newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila urges new law to lure investors leaving HK.
newsitem.headline: Manila urges new law to lure investors leaving HK.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Sunday called on the Congress to immediately pass a law that would grant incentives to businesses that might leave Hong Kong after its handover to China on July 1.
Passage of such a law is one of the measures that would help the Philippines "pole vault into the 21st century," a presidential palace news release quoted Ramos as saying.

"In preparation for China's take-over of Hong Kong, the president asked the legislators to immediately pass the bill granting incentives to multinational corporations and their regional headquarters," the palace statement said.
The palace did not specify what incentives Ramos was seeking.

Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said recently the administration wanted several laws changed to make foreign investments in the country easier as part of what he called "the Hongkongisation programme".
The phrase derives from Manila's hope that many businesses would leave the British colony after it reverts to Chinese rule.
Ramos also urged the Congress to abolish laws that permit monopolies as well as government policies "that tend to abet the concentration of economic power in the hands of the oligarchy".
Ramos has been credited by economists and diplomats with turning the economy around by launching a series of reforms that have liberalised the banking, energy and telecommunications sectors.
